paper.title_en: Faithful filtering of constrained quantum records: Local limits and collective advantage from loops
paper.abstract_en: Weak probes can record whether neighboring spins are aligned without revealing their common orientation. Reading the probes can then herald a projection of an unknown spin state onto the aligned subspace that preserves every coherence within it. We ask how often this projection succeeds when the probes are read separately or jointly. For binary pure product records and zero false positives, we derive the exact optimum over all separable measurements, and hence over all local operations and classical communication. It is the probability that one-sided local witnesses exclude every alternative, and simultaneous local measurements attain it. Joint readout can do better by accepting coherent combinations of ambiguous outcomes in which the alternatives cancel. For pairwise parity records on a connected simple graph, it beats every local strategy exactly when the graph has a loop, at all record overlaps strictly between zero and one. For general binary linear records, the condition is an irreducible dependency among at least three records. The advantage lowers the leading power of the efficiency at weak recording. On a triangle the efficiency becomes linear rather than quadratic in the witness probability, and a three-pulse coherent-light receiver captures this gain with a single click. Extensions treat targets spanning several patterns and a noisy comparison at a common output fidelity.
